name: P1 · KRIES A — Current Affairs (ಪ್ರಚಲಿತ ವಿದ್ಯಮಾನಗಳು)
description: All topics so far (45 sets × 20 questions): International Affairs and Organisations; National Affairs, Schemes and Defence; Karnataka Current Affairs; National Current Affairs – Month by Month; Awards, Books, Films and Sports; Important Days and Events; KEA Previous-Year Questions – Current Affairs. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

subjects.name: P1 · KRIES A – Current Affairs (ಪ್ರಚಲಿತ ವಿದ್ಯಮಾನಗಳು)

questions.question:
Which are the member-countries of Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QUAD)?
a) India
b) Japan
c) USA
d) Australia

questions.subject: Organisations, Summits and Diplomacy

questions.question:

questions.question:
Consider the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine, 2025.
(a) This was awarded by the Nobel Assembly at Pasteur Institute
(b) The award was given to a group of 3 Scientists
(c) Contribution was discovery of Peripheral immune tolerance and identification of Regulatory T Cells and FOXP3 genes
(d) The contribution will help in treating diseases like Cardiac arrest and Obesity.
How many of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.subject: World Events, Awards and Sports
questions.explanation: (b) and (c) are correct (Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, Shimon Sakaguchi). The medicine prize is awarded by the Nobel Assembly at the Karolinska Institutet, and the work matters for autoimmune diseases, cancer and transplants. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: World Events, Awards and Sports

questions.question:
WHO declares Monkeypox (Mpox) outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. In this regard which of the following statements are correct?
a) Monkeypox virus belongs to the same family of viruses as smallpox virus
b) This disease spreads through direct skin-to-skin contact
c) It is a zoonotic disease also
d) Monkeypox variants are called as clades

options.A: Only a and c are correct
options.B: Only a, b and c are correct
options.C: Only a, c and d are correct
options.D: a, b, c and d are correct

questions.subject: World Events, Awards and Sports
questions.explanation: Mpox is an orthopoxvirus (like smallpox), zoonotic, spread by close contact, and its variants are called clades (Ib caused the 2024 emergency). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: World Events, Awards and Sports

questions.question: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of United Nations had decided which of the following year as International Year of Millets?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports

questions.question: Which of the following organisation brings out the publication known as "World Economic Outlook"?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook twice a year (April and October). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: The reserve tranche is the part of a member's IMF quota paid in reserve assets; the member can draw it without conditions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Expand UNODA.

options.B: United Nations Office for Disarmament Affairs
options.C: United Nations Office for Defence Arms
options.D: United Nations Office for Deficiency Affairs

questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: UNODA (New York) supports disarmament work, including the Arms Trade Treaty and weapons of mass destruction. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Indicate the correct chronological order for the setting up of the following institutions.
(a) GATT
(b) IMF
(c) European Union
(d) WTO
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: IMF – December 1945; GATT – signed 1947 (in force 1948); European Union – Maastricht Treaty, 1993; WTO – 1 January 1995. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:

a. International Monetary Fund (IMF) – 27th December, 1945
b. Multilateral Investment Guaranty Agency (MIGA) – 1988
c. New Development Bank or BRICS Bank – 2012
d. Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) – 2020
How many pairs in the above are correctly matched ?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: IMF (27 Dec 1945) and MIGA (1988) are right. The NDB was agreed at Fortaleza in 2014 (working from 2015) and the AIIB started in January 2016. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which organizations conducted jointly the Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) in 2025?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: The FSAP, started in 1999, is a joint IMF–World Bank review of a country's financial sector; India's latest was released in 2025. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The United Nations Organization came into existence on:
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC / SSC GK). The Charter was signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945 and came into force on 24 October 1945 (UN Day).

questions.question: Which principal organ of the UN has five permanent members with veto power?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: The P5 are China, France, Russia, the UK and the USA; the other 10 members are elected for two years.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, is located at:
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC / SSC GK). It has 15 judges elected for nine years; it is the only principal organ outside New York.

questions.question: Which principal organ of the UN suspended its operations in 1994 after the last trust territory, Palau, became independent?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: The UN has six principal organs in the Charter.

questions.question:

a. UNESCO
b. FAO
c. IAEA
d. UNEP

1. Rome
2. Vienna
3. Nairobi
4. Paris
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC / SSC GK). UNEP (1972) is the first UN agency headquartered in a developing country.

questions.question: Which of these UN bodies is headquartered in Geneva?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports

questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: ITU (Geneva) – 1865; UPU (Bern) – 1874; ILO (Geneva) – 1919.

questions.question: The International Labour Organization, which won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969, was set up in:
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: It became the first specialised agency of the UN in 1946 and has a tripartite structure (governments, employers, workers).

questions.question: Who was the first woman President of the UN General Assembly?
questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KPSC / SSC GK). She presided over the 8th session (1953). Hansa Mehta helped draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:

questions.subject: The UN System – Organs, Agencies and Reports
questions.explanation: India signed the Charter in 1945 even before independence; its eighth term was 2021–22.

questions.question:

notes.md:
# Current international affairs (2024 – mid-2026)

> How to use: read once, then revise the tables. KEA asks *who / where / which country / which edition*. Facts are as reported up to mid-2026; check the newspaper for anything newer.

## 1. Groupings and summits
| Grouping | Members / key facts | Recent summit (host) |
|---|---|---|
| **G20** | 19 countries + EU + **African Union** (permanent member since New Delhi summit, Sept 2023) | 2023 New Delhi (India) · 2024 Rio de Janeiro (Brazil) · **2025 Johannesburg (South Africa) – first in Africa** · 2026 USA |
| **BRICS** | Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE (2024) + **Indonesia (Jan 2025)** | 2024 Kazan (Russia) · **2025 Rio de Janeiro (Brazil)** · **2026 – India chairs** |
| **SCO** | 10 members: China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran (2023), **Belarus (4 July 2024, Astana)** | 2024 Astana · **2025 Tianjin (China)** |
| **Quad** | India, Japan, USA, Australia | — |
| **I2U2** ("West Asian Quad") | India, Israel, USA, UAE | Common with Quad: **India & USA** |
| **UN Peacebuilding Commission** | Set up **2005**; India a **founding member**; re-elected for 2025–26 | Link between UNGA and UNSC |
| **WTO Ministerial** | MC13 Abu Dhabi (2024) · **MC14 Yaoundé, Cameroon (March 2026)** | |
| **UN Climate (COP)** | COP28 Dubai (2023) · COP29 Baku (2024) · **COP30 Belém, Brazil (Nov 2025)** | |

## 2. United Nations
- **Secretary-General:** António Guterres (Portugal), 9th SG, since 2017. Earlier: Trygve Lie (Norway, 1st), U Thant (Myanmar), Kurt Waldheim (Austria), **Javier Pérez de Cuéllar (Peru)**, Boutros Boutros-Ghali (Egypt), Kofi Annan (Ghana), Ban Ki-moon (South Korea).
- **President, 80th UNGA (2025–26):** Annalena Baerbock (Germany).
- WHO: **Pandemic Agreement** adopted by the World Health Assembly, **May 2025**. Mpox declared a public-health emergency of international concern in **Aug 2024** (clade Ib).

## 3. Leaders in the news
| Country | Leader (post, from) |

| USA | Donald Trump – 47th President (20 Jan 2025) |
| Vatican | **Pope Leo XIV** (Robert Prevost, elected 8 May 2025 – first American Pope) |
| Sri Lanka | Anura Kumara Dissanayake – President (Sept 2024), **JVP / NPP** |
| Canada | Mark Carney – PM (March 2025) |

| South Korea | Lee Jae-myung – President (June 2025) |
| UK | Keir Starmer – PM (July 2024) |

## 4. Trade deals
- **India–UK CETA** signed **24 July 2025**.
- **India–EFTA TEPA** in force **1 Oct 2025** (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein).
- **India–EU FTA** – called the **"mother of all deals"**, concluded **27 Jan 2026**; the EU leaders **António Costa** and **Ursula von der Leyen** were chief guests on Republic Day 2026.

## 5. Nobel Prizes
| Year | Peace | Literature | Medicine | Physics | Chemistry | Economics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | Narges Mohammadi (Iran) | Jon Fosse | **Karikó & Weissman (mRNA vaccines)** | Agostini, Krausz, L'Huillier (attosecond) | Bawendi, Brus, Ekimov (quantum dots) | Claudia Goldin |
| 2024 | Nihon Hidankyo (Japan) | Han Kang (S. Korea) | Ambros & Ruvkun (microRNA) | Hopfield & **Hinton** (AI) | Baker, Hassabis, Jumper (proteins) | Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson |

notes.title: United Nations – organs, agencies, headquarters (detailed)
notes.md:
# United Nations Organization (UNO)

## 1. Basics
| Point | Fact |
|---|---|
| Idea | **Atlantic Charter** (1941, Roosevelt & Churchill) → **Declaration by United Nations** (1 Jan 1942) – name coined by **F. D. Roosevelt** |
| Planning | Dumbarton Oaks (1944), Yalta (Feb 1945) |
| Charter signed | **26 June 1945**, **San Francisco** (50 countries; Poland signed later → **51 founding members**) |
| Came into existence | **24 October 1945** → **UN Day** |
| Members | **193** (latest: **South Sudan, 2011**); observers: Holy See, Palestine |
| Headquarters | **New York** (land donated by John D. Rockefeller Jr.); other offices: Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi |
| Official languages | **6** – Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, Spanish (Arabic added 1973); working languages: English, French |
| Predecessor | **League of Nations** (1920, Geneva; dissolved 1946) |
| India | **Founding member** (signed in 1945, before independence) |

## 2. Six principal organs
| Organ | Key facts |
|---|---|
| **General Assembly** | All 193 members, one vote each; President elected yearly. 80th session (2025–26) President: **Annalena Baerbock** (Germany). First woman President: **Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit** (India, 1953) |
| **Security Council** | **15 members**: 5 permanent with **veto** (**USA, UK, France, Russia, China**) + 10 non-permanent elected for **2 years**. India – non-permanent **8 times** (last **2021–22**); seeks a permanent seat (with Brazil, Germany, Japan = **G4**) |
| **Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)** | **54 members**, 3-year terms; coordinates the specialised agencies |
| **Trusteeship Council** | Suspended **1 Nov 1994** after **Palau** became independent |
| **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** | **The Hague**, Netherlands – the only principal organ outside New York; **15 judges**, **9-year** terms. Indian judges: B. N. Rau, Nagendra Singh (President 1985–88), R. S. Pathak, **Dalveer Bhandari** |
| **Secretariat** | Headed by the **Secretary-General** – appointed by the GA on the SC's recommendation, 5-year term |

## 3. Secretaries-General
| # | Name | Country | Term |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trygve Lie | Norway | 1946–52 |
| 2 | Dag Hammarskjöld | Sweden | 1953–61 (died in a plane crash; posthumous Nobel) |
| 3 | **U Thant** | **Myanmar (Burma)** | 1961–71 – first Asian |
| 4 | Kurt Waldheim | Austria | 1972–81 |
| 5 | **Javier Pérez de Cuéllar** | **Peru** | 1982–91 |
| 6 | Boutros Boutros-Ghali | Egypt | 1992–96 – first African |
| 7 | Kofi Annan | Ghana | 1997–2006 (Nobel 2001 with the UN) |
| 8 | Ban Ki-moon | South Korea | 2007–16 |
| 9 | **António Guterres** | **Portugal** | 2017–**31 Dec 2026**; selection of the 10th SG is under way in 2026 |

**Trap:** VAO 2024 swapped Pérez de Cuéllar (Peru) and Guterres (Portugal).

## 4. Specialised agencies and other UN bodies – headquarters
| Body | HQ | Set up | Remember |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ITU** – International Telecommunication Union | Geneva | **1865** | Oldest; World Telecom Day 17 May |
| **UPU** – Universal Postal Union | **Bern** | 1874 | World Post Day 9 Oct |
| **ILO** – International Labour Organization | Geneva | **1919** (Treaty of Versailles) | Tripartite; **Nobel Peace 1969**; first UN specialised agency (1946) |
| **FAO** – Food and Agriculture Organization | **Rome** | 1945 (16 Oct = World Food Day) | Led the **International Year of Millets 2023** (India's proposal) |
| **UNESCO** – Educational, Scientific and Cultural Org. | **Paris** | 1945 (in force 1946) | World Heritage list; GEM Report |
| **WHO** – World Health Organization | **Geneva** | **7 April 1948** (World Health Day) | Pandemic Agreement adopted May 2025; USA withdrew in Jan 2026 |
| **IMF** – International Monetary Fund | **Washington D.C.** | Bretton Woods 1944; **27 Dec 1945** | **World Economic Outlook**, Global Financial Stability Report; SDR, reserve tranche |
| **World Bank** (IBRD) | Washington D.C. | 1944/45 | **World Development Report**; IDA (1960), IFC (1956), **MIGA (1988)**, ICSID |
| **WTO** – World Trade Organization | **Geneva** | **1 Jan 1995** (replaced GATT, 1947/48) | Marrakesh Agreement 1994; not a UN agency (related organisation) |
| **IAEA** – International Atomic Energy Agency | **Vienna** | 1957 | "Atoms for Peace"; Nobel 2005 |
| **UNIDO**, **UNODC** | Vienna | 1966 / 1997 | Industrial development / drugs and crime |
| **WMO** – World Meteorological Organization | Geneva | 1950 (23 March) | With UNEP set up the **IPCC** (1988) |
| **WIPO** – World Intellectual Property Org. | Geneva | 1967 | **Global Innovation Index** |
| **ICAO** – International Civil Aviation Org. | **Montreal** | 1944 (Chicago Convention), 1947 | |
| **IMO** – International Maritime Org. | **London** | 1948 | Only UN agency HQ in the UK |
| **IFAD**, **WFP** | **Rome** | 1977 / 1961 | WFP – **Nobel Peace 2020** |
| **UN Tourism** (UNWTO) | **Madrid** | 1975 | |
| **UNEP** – UN Environment Programme | **Nairobi** | **1972** (Stockholm conference) | First UN HQ in a developing country; Emissions Gap Report |
| **UN-Habitat** | Nairobi | 1978 | |
| **UNICEF** | New York | 1946 | Nobel 1965 |
| **UNDP** | New York | 1965 | **Human Development Report** (HDI) |
| **UNFPA** | New York | 1969 | State of World Population |
| **UN Women** | New York | 2010 | |
| **UNODA** – Office for **Disarmament Affairs** | New York | 1998 (as department 1982) | |
| **UNHCR** – Refugee agency | Geneva | 1950 | Nobel 1954 and 1981 |
| **UNCTAD** | Geneva | 1964 | **World Investment Report** |
| **UNFCCC** secretariat | **Bonn** | 1992 (Rio) | COPs; Paris Agreement 2015 |
| **UN University** | **Tokyo** | 1973 | |

## 5. Other international organisations
| Organisation | HQ | Founded | Members / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **NATO** | **Brussels** | 1949 (Washington Treaty) | **32**: Finland **31st** (Apr 2023), **Sweden 32nd** (Mar 2024); Art. 5 – collective defence |
| **ASEAN** | **Jakarta** | 1967 (Bangkok Declaration) | **11** – **Timor-Leste** joined Oct 2025 |
| **African Union** | **Addis Ababa** | 2002 (OAU 1963) | 55; joined **G20** in 2023 |
| **European Union** | Brussels | 1993 (Maastricht) | 27 (UK left 2020); euro |
| **SAARC** | **Kathmandu** | 1985 (Dhaka) | 8 – Afghanistan joined 2007 |
| **BIMSTEC** | **Dhaka** | 1997 | 7: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand – **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation** |
| **OPEC** | **Vienna** | 1960 (**Baghdad**) | Qatar left 2019, Ecuador 2020, Angola 2024 |
| **G20** | No secretariat | 1999 | 19 countries + EU + AU; India presidency 2023 (New Delhi) |
| **BRICS / NDB** | NDB: **Shanghai** | 2009 / NDB 2014–15 | Indonesia full member Jan 2025; India chairs BRICS in 2026 |
| **AIIB** | **Beijing** | **2016** | India is the 2nd largest shareholder |
| **ADB** | **Manila** | 1966 | |
| **SCO** | Beijing (secretariat) | 2001 | 10 members – Iran 2023, Belarus 2024 |
| **Commonwealth** | London | 1949 (London Declaration) | 56 members – Gabon and Togo joined 2022 |
| **OECD** | Paris | 1961 | International Migration Outlook |
| **WEF** | Cologny, Geneva | 1971 | Davos meeting; Global Gender Gap, Global Risks reports |
| **INTERPOL** | **Lyon** | 1923 | Europol – The Hague |
| **ICRC** (Red Cross) | Geneva | 1863 (Henry Dunant) | Nobel 1917, 1944, 1963 |
| **Amnesty International** | London | 1961 | Nobel 1977 |
| **IUCN** | **Gland**, Switzerland | 1948 | **Red List** of threatened species (extinction risk) |
| **WWF** | Gland, Switzerland | 1961 | **Earth Hour** – started in **Sydney, 2007**, last Saturday of March (not UNEP!) |
| **International Solar Alliance** | **Gurugram**, India | 2015 (India + **France**, COP21 Paris) | Not all SAARC states are members |
| **ICC** (International Criminal Court) | The Hague | 2002 (Rome Statute) | India is not a member |
| **Quad** | – | 2007, revived 2017 | India, USA, Japan, Australia – informal dialogue, no defence treaty |

## 6. Who publishes which report?
| Report / index | Publisher |
|---|---|
| World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report | **IMF** |
| World Development Report | **World Bank** |
| Human Development Report | **UNDP** |
| World Investment Report | **UNCTAD** |
| Global Education Monitoring Report | **UNESCO** |
| International Migration Outlook | **OECD** |
| Global Gender Gap, Global Risks | **WEF** |
| Index of Economic Freedom | **Heritage Foundation** (with the Wall Street Journal) |
| Global Peace Index | Institute for Economics and Peace |
| Corruption Perceptions Index | Transparency International (Berlin) |
| World Press Freedom Index | Reporters Without Borders (Paris) |
| Global Innovation Index | **WIPO** |
| Living Planet Report | WWF |
| Emissions Gap Report | UNEP |
| World Happiness Report | Wellbeing Research Centre (Oxford) with Gallup and UN SDSN |
| State of Food Security and Nutrition | FAO (with IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, WHO) |
| Financial Sector Assessment Program (FSAP) | **IMF + World Bank** jointly |

## 7. Heads (as of mid-2026 – these change, check before the exam)
UN SG **António Guterres** · WHO **Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus** · IMF **Kristalina Georgieva** · World Bank **Ajay Banga** · WTO **Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala** (2nd term from Sept 2025) · IAEA **Rafael Grossi** · ILO **Gilbert Houngbo** · FAO **Qu Dongyu** · UNEP **Inger Andersen** · ITU **Doreen Bogdan-Martin**.

## 8. Traps and confusions
- UN came into existence **24 Oct 1945**; the Charter was signed **26 June 1945**.
- **WTO** (trade, Geneva) vs **UN Tourism** (formerly UNWTO, Madrid).
- **UNEP – Nairobi**, not Geneva; **UPU – Bern**, not Geneva; **IMO – London**; **ICAO – Montreal**.
- **Earth Hour** – WWF, not UNEP. **ISA** – India + France, HQ Gurugram (not Bonn; Bonn hosts the UNFCCC).
- **GATT (1947)** came before the WTO (1995); the IMF (1945) came before GATT.
- **NDB** agreed 2014 (Fortaleza), **AIIB** started 2016 – not 2012 / 2020.

notes.title: India's foreign relations – detailed notes
notes.md:
# India's foreign relations

## 1. Principles
- **Panchsheel** (1954, India–China): mutual respect for territory and sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, peaceful coexistence.
- **Non-Alignment:** Nehru, **Nasser** (Egypt), **Tito** (Yugoslavia) at **Brioni (1956)**; NAM founded at **Belgrade (1961)** with **Sukarno** (Indonesia) and **Nkrumah** (Ghana).
- **Neighbourhood First** · **SAGAR** (2015, Indian Ocean) · **Look East (1991) → Act East (2014)** · **Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam** – G20 theme "One Earth, One Family, One Future".
- **Strategic autonomy**: India deals with the USA, Russia and others at the same time.

## 2. Groupings (India's status)
| Grouping | India |
|---|---|
| G20 | Member; **New Delhi summit, Sept 2023** (African Union admitted) |
| G7 | **Invited guest only** |
| BRICS / **NDB** | Founder; BRICS expanded 2024–25 |
| **SCO** | Full member since **2017**; chair 2023 |
| Quad | India, USA, Japan, Australia |
| SAARC (1985) / BIMSTEC (1997) | Founder |
| **ISA** | Launched by India & France at **COP21 Paris, 2015**; HQ **Gurugram** |
| CARICOM | Caribbean grouping; **2nd India–CARICOM Summit, Georgetown (Guyana), Nov 2024** |
| UN Security Council | Non-permanent member 8 times; seeks a permanent seat |

G20 venues: 2008 Washington · 2021 Rome · **2022 Bali** · 2023 New Delhi · 2024 Rio de Janeiro · 2025 Johannesburg.

## 3. Treaties and agreements
| Year | Agreement |
|---|---|
| 1954 | Panchsheel (China) |
| 1960 | **Indus Waters Treaty** (World Bank) – **in abeyance from April 2025** |
| 1966 | Tashkent Declaration (Shastri–Ayub) |
| 1971 | Indo-Soviet Treaty of Friendship |
| 1972 | **Simla Agreement** (Indira–Bhutto) |
| 1987 | India–Sri Lanka Accord (IPKF) |
| 2008 | India–US civil nuclear (123) agreement |
| 2015 | India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (enclaves) |
| 2022 | **CEPA with UAE**; ECTA with Australia |
| 2024 | **TEPA with EFTA** (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein); Chabahar 10-year deal |
| 2025 | **India–UK trade agreement** (July) |

## 4. Neighbours
- **Pakistan:** wars 1947, 1965, 1971, 1999 (Kargil); Kartarpur Corridor 2019; **Operation Sindoor** May 2025.
- **China:** 1962 war; LAC; **Galwan** clash June 2020; disengagement agreement Oct 2024.
- **Bangladesh:** longest border (~4,096 km); Maitri Setu (Tripura).
- **Nepal:** Kalapani–Lipulekh dispute; open border. **Bhutan:** hydropower. **Sri Lanka:** Katchatheevu (1974); IPKF (1987).
- **Maldives:** 'India Out' campaign, then a reset in 2024–25. **Myanmar:** Kaladan project; **Operation Brahma** (2025 quake).

## 5. Other partners
USA – 2+2 dialogue, iCET, Quad · Russia – S-400, Kudankulam, BrahMos · Japan – bullet train · France – Rafale, ISA · Iran – **Chabahar** · Gulf – IMEC (G20 2023).

## 6. Evacuations
Rahat (Yemen 2015) · Devi Shakti (Afghanistan 2021) · Ganga (Ukraine 2022) · Kaveri (Sudan 2023) · Ajay (Israel 2023) · **Sindhu** (Iran/Israel 2025).

## 7. Traps
- India is **not** a G7 member. ISA HQ is in **Gurugram**, not Bengaluru.
- Zhou Enlai was at **Bandung (1955)**, not a NAM founder.

notes.title: National affairs 2024–26 – revision notes
notes.md:
# Current national affairs (2024 – mid-2026)

## 1. Constitutional and key posts (as of early 2026)
| Post | Holder |
|---|---|
| President | Droupadi Murmu (15th, July 2022) |
| Vice-President | **C. P. Radhakrishnan** (15th, Sept 2025 – after Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned in July 2025) |
| Prime Minister | Narendra Modi (third term, June 2024) |
| Chief Justice of India | **Surya Kant** (53rd, 24 Nov 2025); before him B. R. Gavai (52nd) |
| Chief Election Commissioner | Gyanesh Kumar (Feb 2025) |
| RBI Governor | Sanjay Malhotra (Dec 2024) |
| Union Minister of Cooperation | **Amit Shah** (also Home) – ministry created 2021 |
| Karnataka CM | Siddaramaiah – equalled **D. Devaraj Urs's record of 2,792 days** on 6 Jan 2026 |

## 2. Republic Day chief guests
2024 – Emmanuel Macron (France) · 2025 – Prabowo Subianto (Indonesia) · **2026 (77th) – António Costa & Ursula von der Leyen (EU)**.

## 3. Defence and security
- **Operation Sindoor** (7 May 2025): strikes on terror camps in Pakistan & PoK after the **Pahalgam attack** (22 Apr 2025).
- Evacuation operations: Ganga (Ukraine 2022), Kaveri (Sudan 2023), Ajay (Israel 2023), Indravati (Haiti 2024).
- INS Vikrant – first indigenous aircraft carrier (2022).

## 4. Space
| Mission | Fact |
|---|---|
| Chandrayaan-3 | Landed near lunar south pole **23 Aug 2023** → **National Space Day (first observed 23 Aug 2024)** |
| Aditya-L1 | Solar observatory at L1 (launched Sept 2023) |
| **Axiom-4** | **Shubhanshu Shukla** – first Indian on the ISS (June 2025) |
| **NISAR** | NASA–ISRO radar satellite, GSLV-F16, **30 July 2025** |
| **CMS-03** | **Communication** satellite (~4,400 kg) by **LVM3-M5, 2 Nov 2025** – heaviest launched from India |

## 5. Economy, laws and schemes
- **GST 2.0** (22 Sept 2025): two main slabs **5% and 18%** (+40% on luxury / sin goods).
- **Four Labour Codes** in force from **21 Nov 2025**.
- **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025**. Next **Census with caste enumeration** (reference date 1 March 2027).
- **Kerala** – first state declared **free of extreme poverty** (1 Nov 2025).
- **PMSBY** – accident insurance (₹2 lakh) · **PMJJBY** – life insurance · **MUDRA** – Shishu / Kishor / Tarun (+ Tarun Plus up to ₹20 lakh) · **AMRUT** – Atal Mission for **Rejuvenation** and Urban **Transformation** (2015) · **PM-JANMAN** (2023) – PVTGs.
- **Maha Kumbh 2025** – Prayagraj, 13 Jan – 26 Feb 2025.
- Karnataka's **five guarantees** (2023): Gruha Jyothi (free power up to 200 units), Gruha Lakshmi (₹2,000/month to women heads), Anna Bhagya (rice), **Shakti (free bus travel for women)**, Yuva Nidhi (unemployment allowance).

## 6. Awards and people
- **Bharat Ratna 2024:** Karpoori Thakur, L. K. Advani, P. V. Narasimha Rao, Charan Singh, **M. S. Swaminathan** (also Padma Shri 1967, Magsaysay 1971, Albert Einstein World Science Award 1986).
- **Kendra Sahitya Akademi 2024 (Kannada):** **K. V. Narayana – *Nudigala Alivu***.
- **Surekha Yadav** – Asia's first woman loco pilot, retired Sept 2025.
- **Aditi Swami & Ojas Deotale** – India's first individual world titles in compound **archery** (2023).

## 7. Sports (national angle)
Paris 2024: 6 medals · Asia Cup 2025 – India beat Pakistan in Dubai (28 Sept 2025) · Women's ODI World Cup 2025 – India champions · Divya Deshmukh – FIDE Women's World Cup 2025.

notes.title: Indian Army, Navy and Air Force – detailed notes
notes.md:
# Three wings of the armed forces

## 1. Command and heads
- **Supreme Commander:** the **President** (Art. 53). **Defence Minister** heads the Ministry of Defence.
- **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS):** post created 2019; heads the **Department of Military Affairs**; first CDS **Gen Bipin Rawat** (1 Jan 2020, died Dec 2021); then **Gen Anil Chauhan** (from Sept 2022).
- Service chiefs as of 2025: Army – **Gen Upendra Dwivedi**; Navy – **Adm Dinesh K. Tripathi**; Air Force – **ACM A. P. Singh** (check for changes).
- All three service headquarters are in **New Delhi**.

## 2. Days
| Day | Date | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Army Day** | **15 Jan** | Gen **K. M. Cariappa** became first Indian C-in-C (1949) |
| **Air Force Day** | **8 Oct** | IAF founded 1932 |
| **Navy Day** | **4 Dec** | **Operation Trident** (Karachi, 1971) |
| Armed Forces Flag Day | 7 Dec | |
| **Kargil Vijay Diwas** | **26 Jul** | Op Vijay 1999 |
| **Vijay Diwas** | **16 Dec** | 1971 victory, Bangladesh |
| Territorial Army Day | 9 Oct | |

## 3. Rank equivalents
| Army | Navy | Air Force |
|---|---|---|
| General | Admiral | Air Chief Marshal |
| Lieutenant General | Vice Admiral | Air Marshal |
| Major General | Rear Admiral | Air Vice Marshal |
| Brigadier | Commodore | Air Commodore |
| Colonel | Captain | Group Captain |
| Lieutenant Colonel | Commander | Wing Commander |
| Major | Lieutenant Commander | Squadron Leader |
| Captain | Lieutenant | Flight Lieutenant |
| Lieutenant | Sub Lieutenant | Flying Officer |
**Five-star ranks:** Field Marshal **Sam Manekshaw** (1973) and **K. M. Cariappa** (1986, from **Kodagu**); Marshal of the IAF **Arjan Singh** (2002).

## 4. Commands
- **Army (7):** Northern (Udhampur), Western (Chandimandir), South Western (Jaipur), Southern (Pune), Central (Lucknow), Eastern (Kolkata), Army Training Command (Shimla).
- **Navy (3):** **Western – Mumbai**, **Eastern – Visakhapatnam**, Southern – Kochi (training). Andaman & Nicobar Command (Port Blair) is tri-service.
- **Air Force (7):** Western (New Delhi), Eastern (Shillong), Central (Prayagraj), South Western (Gandhinagar), Southern (Thiruvananthapuram), **Training – Bengaluru**, Maintenance – Nagpur.

## 5. Training and recruitment
NDA **Khadakwasla (Pune)** · IMA **Dehradun** · Indian Naval Academy **Ezhimala** (Kerala) · Air Force Academy **Dundigal** (Hyderabad) · OTA Chennai and Gaya · Sainik Schools (Karnataka: **Kodagu – Kudige**, **Vijayapura**). **Agnipath** (2022): Agniveers serve **4 years**, up to **25%** retained. **NCC** – 1948.

## 6. Gallantry awards
Wartime: **Param Vir Chakra** > Maha Vir Chakra > Vir Chakra. Peacetime: **Ashoka Chakra** > Kirti Chakra > Shaurya Chakra. First PVC: **Major Somnath Sharma** (1947).

## 7. Equipment
| Item | Facts |
|---|---|
| **INS Vikrant** | First indigenous aircraft carrier, **Cochin Shipyard**, commissioned **2 Sep 2022** |
| INS Vikramaditya | Carrier bought from Russia |
| **INS Arihant** | First indigenous nuclear ballistic-missile submarine |
| **INS Kadamba, Karwar** | Project Seabird naval base (Karnataka) |
| **Tejas** | Light Combat Aircraft – **HAL Bengaluru** |
| Rafale | France (Dassault) |
| **Prachand** | Light Combat Helicopter (2022) |
| Arjun | Main battle tank |
| **BrahMos** | Supersonic cruise missile – **India + Russia** |
| Agni / Agni Prime | Ballistic missiles; Agni-V ~5,000 km; **Agni Prime** tested June 2023 |
| Prithvi, Akash, Nag, Trishul | IGMDP (1983, Dr Kalam); **DRDO** founded **1958** |

## 8. Paramilitary and others
- **CAPFs (Home Ministry):** CRPF (largest), BSF (1965), CISF, ITBP, SSB; **Assam Rifles** – oldest (1835).
- **Indian Coast Guard** – 1977, **Ministry of Defence**.

## 9. Operations
| Operation | What |
|---|---|
| Vijay | Goa 1961; Kargil 1999 |
| Trident | Karachi harbour 1971 |
| **Meghdoot** | Siachen 1984 |
| Blue Star | Golden Temple 1984 |
| Ganga / Kaveri / Ajay | Evacuations: Ukraine 2022 / Sudan 2023 / Israel 2023 |
| **Brahma** | Myanmar earthquake relief, March 2025 |
| **Sindoor** | Strikes after the **Pahalgam attack**, May 2025 |
| Sindhu | Evacuation from Iran and Israel, June 2025 |
| Black Forest | Anti-Naxal operation, 2025 |

## 10. Joint exercises
| Exercise | With |
|---|---|
| **Varuna** | France (navy) |
| Garuda / Shakti | France (air / army) |
| **Malabar** | USA, Japan, Australia (navies) |

| **Indra** | Russia |
| **Dharma Guardian** | Japan (army) |

| SIMBEX | Singapore (navy) |
| **Cyclone** | Egypt |
| Nomadic Elephant | Mongolia |

| Tarang Shakti | IAF multinational (2024) |

## 11. Traps
- Army Day 15 Jan, Navy Day 4 Dec, **Air Force Day 8 Oct** – don't mix them up.
- Ashoka Chakra = **peacetime**; PVC = **wartime**.
- Coast Guard is under **Defence**, CAPFs under **Home**.
- Varuna = France, Indra = Russia, Surya Kiran = Nepal, Cyclone = Egypt.

notes.title: Karnataka and national affairs – detailed notes (2023 – mid-2026)
notes.md:
# Current state and national affairs

> Office-holders change – check the latest before the exam.

## Karnataka – who's who
| Post | Name |
|---|---|
| Governor | **Thaawarchand Gehlot** (July 2021) |
| Chief Minister | **D. K. Shivakumar** (sworn in **3 June 2026**) – Deputy CM **G. Parameshwara** |
| Previous CM | **Siddaramaiah** (May 2023 – resigned May 2026; longest-serving CM, Jan 2026) |
| Council Chairman | Basavaraj Horatti |
| VGIT chair (Jan 2026) | **Kris Gopalakrishnan** |
U. T. Khader, Speaker 2023–26, became Health Minister in the Shivakumar ministry.

## Five guarantees (2023)
| Scheme | Benefit |
|---|---|
| **Shakti** (11 June 2023) | Free bus travel for women in state buses |
| **Gruha Jyothi** | Up to **200 units** free electricity |
| **Gruha Lakshmi** | **₹2,000/month** to woman head of family |
| **Anna Bhagya** | 10 kg grain (5 kg rice + cash) |
| **Yuva Nidhi** | ₹3,000 (graduates) / ₹1,500 (diploma) a month to the unemployed |

## Governance and places
- **Greater Bengaluru Authority** replaced BBMP (2025), with **five corporations**.
- **Ramanagara → Bengaluru South** district (2025). Karnataka has 31 districts (Vijayanagara the 31st, 2021).
- **Kalyana Karnataka** (renamed 2019): Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal, Ballari, Vijayanagara; **Kalyana Karnataka Utsava – 17 Sept**; Article **371J** (2012).
- **Arivu Kendras** – upgraded Gram Panchayat libraries. **KTCP** – Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act (1961).
- Caste (socio-educational) survey – Sept–Oct 2025; SC internal reservation – **Justice H. N. Nagamohan Das** commission.
- **Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare)** law – welfare board, welfare fee from aggregators, fines (no prison term).

## Economy, technology
- **Invest Karnataka 2025** (Feb 2025); **GCC Policy 2024–29** – 500 new GCCs, ~3.5 lakh jobs.
- **KDEM – 'Beyond Bengaluru'** clusters; **B-SMILE** – SPV for big Bengaluru infrastructure (tunnel road etc.).
- **Q-City (Quantum City)** – Hesaraghatta; Karnataka Quantum Mission. **KSTePS** – Karnataka Science and Technology Promotion Society.
- Namma Metro **Yellow Line** (R. V. Road – Bommasandra, Electronic City) – Aug 2025.
- Budget 2026-27: **Vasudhamrutha** (eco-friendly, soil-health farming).

## Education and health
- **Odu Karnataka** – reading & arithmetic, classes 4–5; **Nali-Kali** – classes 1–3.
- **Yeshasvini** co-operative health scheme – Chief Patron: **Chief Minister**.

## People, culture, sport
- **Banu Mushtaq** – International Booker 2025, 'Heart Lamp' (tr. **Deepa Bhasthi**); inaugurated **Mysuru Dasara 2025**.
- **Tulsi Gowda** – 'Encyclopedia of the Forest' (Halakki tribe; d. Dec 2024). Saalumarada Thimmakka – tree planter.
- **RCB** – first IPL title, **3 June 2025**; Chinnaswamy stampede 4 June 2025 (Justice D'Cunha inquiry).
- Karnataka Ratna latest: **Puneeth Rajkumar** (posthumous).

## National
| Post / event | Fact |
|---|---|
| President | **Droupadi Murmu** (2022) |
| Vice-President | **C. P. Radhakrishnan** (Sept 2025, after Dhankhar resigned) |
| CJI | **Surya Kant** (24 Nov 2025) after B. R. Gavai |
| CEC | **Gyanesh Kumar** (Feb 2025) |
| RBI Governor | **Sanjay Malhotra** (Dec 2024) |
| CEA | V. Anantha Nageswaran |
| NHRC | Justice V. Ramasubramanian |
| GST 2.0 | 5% and 18% (+40%), from **22 Sept 2025** |
| Labour Codes | In force **21 Nov 2025** (4 codes replace 29 laws) |
| Census | Reference date **1 March 2027**, with caste enumeration |
| Space | **Shubhanshu Shukla** – Axiom-4, ISS (June–July 2025) |
| Cricket | Champions Trophy 2025 (men); **Women's ODI World Cup 2025** (beat South Africa) |
| Ports | World's first **CNG terminal** – Bhavnagar, **Gujarat** |

notes.title: Karnataka and national affairs – detailed notes (2023 – mid-2026)
notes.md:
# Current state and national affairs

> Office-holders change – check the latest before the exam.

## Karnataka – who's who
| Post | Name |
|---|---|
| Governor | **Thaawarchand Gehlot** (July 2021) |
| Chief Minister | **D. K. Shivakumar** (sworn in **3 June 2026**) – Deputy CM **G. Parameshwara** |
| Previous CM | **Siddaramaiah** (May 2023 – resigned May 2026; longest-serving CM, Jan 2026) |
| Council Chairman | Basavaraj Horatti |
| VGIT chair (Jan 2026) | **Kris Gopalakrishnan** |
U. T. Khader, Speaker 2023–26, became Health Minister in the Shivakumar ministry.

## Five guarantees (2023)
| Scheme | Benefit |
|---|---|
| **Shakti** (11 June 2023) | Free bus travel for women in state buses |
| **Gruha Jyothi** | Up to **200 units** free electricity |
| **Gruha Lakshmi** | **₹2,000/month** to woman head of family |
| **Anna Bhagya** | 10 kg grain (5 kg rice + cash) |
| **Yuva Nidhi** | ₹3,000 (graduates) / ₹1,500 (diploma) a month to the unemployed |

## Governance and places
- **Greater Bengaluru Authority** replaced BBMP (2025), with **five corporations**.
- **Ramanagara → Bengaluru South** district (2025). Karnataka has 31 districts (Vijayanagara the 31st, 2021).
- **Kalyana Karnataka** (renamed 2019): Bidar, Kalaburagi, Yadgir, Raichur, Koppal, Ballari, Vijayanagara; **Kalyana Karnataka Utsava – 17 Sept**; Article **371J** (2012).
- **Arivu Kendras** – upgraded Gram Panchayat libraries. **KTCP** – Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act (1961).
- Caste (socio-educational) survey – Sept–Oct 2025; SC internal reservation – **Justice H. N. Nagamohan Das** commission.
- **Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare)** law – welfare board, welfare fee from aggregators, fines (no prison term).

## Economy, technology
- **Invest Karnataka 2025** (Feb 2025); **GCC Policy 2024–29** – 500 new GCCs, ~3.5 lakh jobs.
- **KDEM – 'Beyond Bengaluru'** clusters; **B-SMILE** – SPV for big Bengaluru infrastructure (tunnel road etc.).
- **Q-City (Quantum City)** – Hesaraghatta; Karnataka Quantum Mission. **KSTePS** – Karnataka Science and Technology Promotion Society.
- Namma Metro **Yellow Line** (R. V. Road – Bommasandra, Electronic City) – Aug 2025.
- Budget 2026-27: **Vasudhamrutha** (eco-friendly, soil-health farming).

## Education and health
- **Odu Karnataka** – reading & arithmetic, classes 4–5; **Nali-Kali** – classes 1–3.
- **Yeshasvini** co-operative health scheme – Chief Patron: **Chief Minister**.

## People, culture, sport
- **Banu Mushtaq** – International Booker 2025, 'Heart Lamp' (tr. **Deepa Bhasthi**); inaugurated **Mysuru Dasara 2025**.
- **Tulsi Gowda** – 'Encyclopedia of the Forest' (Halakki tribe; d. Dec 2024). Saalumarada Thimmakka – tree planter.
- **RCB** – first IPL title, **3 June 2025**; Chinnaswamy stampede 4 June 2025 (Justice D'Cunha inquiry).
- Karnataka Ratna latest: **Puneeth Rajkumar** (posthumous).

## National
| Post / event | Fact |
|---|---|
| President | **Droupadi Murmu** (2022) |
| Vice-President | **C. P. Radhakrishnan** (Sept 2025, after Dhankhar resigned) |
| CJI | **Surya Kant** (24 Nov 2025) after B. R. Gavai |
| CEC | **Gyanesh Kumar** (Feb 2025) |
| RBI Governor | **Sanjay Malhotra** (Dec 2024) |
| CEA | V. Anantha Nageswaran |
| NHRC | Justice V. Ramasubramanian |
| GST 2.0 | 5% and 18% (+40%), from **22 Sept 2025** |
| Labour Codes | In force **21 Nov 2025** (4 codes replace 29 laws) |
| Census | Reference date **1 March 2027**, with caste enumeration |
| Space | **Shubhanshu Shukla** – Axiom-4, ISS (June–July 2025) |
| Cricket | Champions Trophy 2025 (men); **Women's ODI World Cup 2025** (beat South Africa) |
| Ports | World's first **CNG terminal** – Bhavnagar, **Gujarat** |

questions.question:
Consider the following statements related to Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar Awards.
(a) They are the National Awards in the field of Science, Technology and Innovation
(b) The awards are given in four categories viz. Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar and Vigyan Team
(c) The awards are given in 13 domains
(d) The Award Ceremony for all categories of awards will be held on 28th February (National Science Day) every year
How many of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.subject: Indian National Awards – Civilian, Gallantry, Literary, Film and Sports
questions.explanation: (a), (b), (c) are correct. The awards are announced on 11 May (National Technology Day) and presented on 23 August (National Space Day), not 28 February. They replaced about 300 older science awards, including the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, from 2024. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

notes.md:
## 1. Civilian awards of India
- **Bharat Ratna** and **Padma** awards – instituted 2 January 1954; order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri
- Bharat Ratna: first (1954) – C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, C. V. Raman; first posthumous – Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966); first woman – Indira Gandhi (1971)
- Foreigners – Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1987), Nelson Mandela (1990); only sportsperson – Sachin Tendulkar (2014)
- Karnataka – M. Visvesvaraya (1955), Bhimsen Joshi (2009), C. N. R. Rao (2014)
- **2024 (five)** – Karpoori Thakur, L. K. Advani, P. V. Narasimha Rao, Charan Singh, M. S. Swaminathan
- Padma awards announced on Republic Day eve; conferred by the President

## 2. Gallantry
| Wartime | Peacetime |
|---|---|
| Param Vir Chakra | Ashoka Chakra |
| Maha Vir Chakra | Kirti Chakra |
| Vir Chakra | Shaurya Chakra |
- First Param Vir Chakra – Major Somnath Sharma (1947)

## 3. Literature
| Award | Key facts |
|---|---|
| Jnanpith | Set up 1961; first 1965 – G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam); Hindi most, **Kannada 8** |
| Kannada Jnanpith | Kuvempu 1967, Bendre 1973, Karanth 1977, Masti 1983, Gokak 1990, Ananthamurthy 1994, Karnad 1998, Kambar 2010 |
| Recent Jnanpith | 58th (2023) Gulzar, Rambhadracharya; 59th (2024) Vinod Kumar Shukla |
| Sahitya Akademi | 1954; 24 languages (22 + English, Rajasthani) |
| Saraswati Samman | K. K. Birla Foundation, 1991 |
| Booker 2025 | David Szalay – 'Flesh' (Kiran Desai shortlisted); 2024 – Samantha Harvey 'Orbital' |
| International Booker 2025 | **Banu Mushtaq – 'Heart Lamp'** (Kannada; translator Deepa Bhasthi); 2022 – Geetanjali Shree 'Tomb of Sand' |

## 4. Cinema, sport, science
- **Dadasaheb Phalke** – 1969, first Devika Rani; Dr. Rajkumar 1995; Mohanlal (for 2023)
- Khel Ratna → **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna** (2021); Arjuna 1961 – players; Dronacharya 1985 – coaches
- **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar** (from 2024): Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva–Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar, Vigyan Team; 13 domains; announced 11 May, presented 23 August
- Gandhi Peace Prize – 1995, ₹1 crore; National Teachers' Award – 5 September
- Oscars 2023 – 'Naatu Naatu' (RRR), 'The Elephant Whisperers'

## 5. International
- **Nobel** – first 1901; Economics from 1969; 10 December; Peace in **Oslo**, rest in Stockholm
- Indians: Tagore 1913, Raman 1930, Mother Teresa 1979, Amartya Sen 1998, Satyarthi 2014, Abhijit Banerjee 2019
- **Nobel 2025**: Peace – María Corina Machado; Literature – László Krasznahorkai; Chemistry – Kitagawa, Robson, Yaghi (MOFs); Physics – Clarke, Devoret, Martinis (quantum tunnelling in circuits); Medicine – Brunkow, Ramsdell, Sakaguchi (regulatory T cells); Economics – Mokyr, Aghion, Howitt (innovation-led growth)
| Award | Field / nickname |
|---|---|
| Ramon Magsaysay | 'Asia's Nobel', Philippines |
| Pulitzer | Journalism, USA |
| Abel / Fields | Mathematics (Fields – under 40, every 4 years) |
| Turing | Computing (ACM) |
| Grammy | Music – Ricky Kej 3 |
| Goldman / Whitley | 'Green Nobel' / 'Green Oscar' |
| Right Livelihood | 'Alternative Nobel' |

## 6. Karnataka
- **Karnataka Ratna** – 1992, first Kuvempu and Dr. Rajkumar; Puneeth Rajkumar 2021 (posthumous)
- **Pampa Award** – 1987, first Kuvempu; Rajyotsava Awards – 1 November
- Nadoja – Kannada University, Hampi; Basava Puraskara – social reform; Kuvempu Rashtriya Puraskar – national literary award

## ⚠ Traps
- Booker ≠ International Booker; Kumari Kamala – Padma **Bhushan** 1970
- Vigyan Puraskar ceremony 23 August, not 28 February
- One Nation, One Election committee – Ram Nath Kovind (not Subhash Kashyap)

## 4. Classical Indian works
Kalidasa – *Abhijnana Shakuntalam*, *Meghaduta*, *Raghuvamsha* · Kautilya – *Arthashastra* · Banabhatta – *Harshacharita*, *Kadambari* · Kalhana – *Rajatarangini* (Sanskrit, Kashmir) · Vishakhadatta – *Mudrarakshasa* · Bharavi – *Kiratarjuniya* · Dandin – *Dashakumaracharita* · **Mahendravarman I – *Mattavilasa Prahasana*** · Hala – *Gatha Saptasati* (Maharashtri **Prakrit**, 700 verses, Arya metre) · Ashvaghosha – *Buddhacharita* · Abul Fazl – *Akbarnama*, *Ain-i-Akbari* · Babur – *Baburnama* (Turki) · Tulsidas – *Ramcharitmanas* · Jayadeva – *Gita Govinda*.

## 5. Modern Indian authors
Tagore – *Gitanjali* (Nobel 1913) · Gandhi – *The Story of My Experiments with Truth*, *Hind Swaraj* · Nehru – *Discovery of India*, *Glimpses of World History* · Ambedkar – *Annihilation of Caste* · A. P. J. Abdul Kalam – *Wings of Fire* · R. K. Narayan – *Malgudi Days*, *The Guide* · Salman Rushdie – *Midnight's Children* (Booker 1981) · Arundhati Roy – *The God of Small Things* (Booker 1997) · Kiran Desai – *The Inheritance of Loss* (2006) · Aravind Adiga – *The White Tiger* (2008) · Vikram Seth – *A Suitable Boy* · Amartya Sen – *The Argumentative Indian* · **Shashi Tharoor – *An Era of Darkness*** · Geetanjali Shree – *Tomb of Sand* (International Booker 2022) · Jyotiba Phule – *Gulamgiri*.

## 6. World classics
Homer – *Iliad*, *Odyssey* · Plato – *The Republic* · Machiavelli – *The Prince* · Cervantes – *Don Quixote* · Shakespeare – *Hamlet*, *Macbeth* · Rousseau – *The Social Contract*, *Emile* · Adam Smith – *The Wealth of Nations* · Darwin – *On the Origin of Species* · Marx – *Das Kapital* · Tolstoy – *War and Peace* · Victor Hugo – *Les Misérables* · Dickens – *Oliver Twist*, *A Tale of Two Cities* · Orwell – *Animal Farm*, *1984* · Anne Frank – *The Diary of a Young Girl* · Mandela – *Long Walk to Freedom*.

## ⚠ Traps
- *Kavirajamarga* is by **Srivijaya**, though written at Amoghavarsha's court.
- Kuvempu's Jnanpith was for *Sri Ramayana Darshanam*, not his novels.
- Ranna was a **Chalukya** court poet; Janna and Harihara were **Hoysala** poets.
- *Mookajjiya Kanasugalu* is by Karanth, not Kuvempu. *Neminatha Purana* is not Janna's.

## 2. Dadasaheb Phalke Award (highest Indian film honour, instituted **1969**; first: **Devika Rani**)
| Award year | Recipient |
|---|---|
| 1995 | **Dr Rajkumar** – first and only Kannada artist so far |
| 2020 | Asha Parekh |
| 2021 | Waheeda Rehman |
| 2022 | Mithun Chakraborty (given Oct 2024) |
| **2023** | **Mohanlal** (announced Sept 2025) |

## 3. Firsts in Indian and Kannada cinema
- *Raja Harishchandra* (1913, Dadasaheb Phalke) – first full-length Indian feature.
- *Alam Ara* (1931, Ardeshir Irani) – first Indian talkie. *Kisan Kanya* (1937) – first colour film.
- ***Sati Sulochana* (1934)** – first Kannada talkie. *Bedara Kannappa* (1954) – Dr Rajkumar's debut as hero.
- *Samskara* (1970, from **U. R. Ananthamurthy**'s novel) – Kannada new wave; *Ghatashraddha* (Girish Kasaravalli); *Nagarahavu* (Puttanna Kanagal, launched Vishnuvardhan); *Ondanondu Kaladalli* (Shankar Nag); *Pushpaka Vimana* (1987, silent film with Kamal Haasan); *Kantara* (2022) & *Kantara: Chapter 1* (2025) – Rishab Shetty.
- Puneeth Rajkumar – "Power Star", posthumous **Karnataka Ratna** (2021).

## 4. Oscars and world festivals
- **Oscars** (Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences, USA; first 1929). Bhanu Athaiya – first Indian winner (costume, *Gandhi*, 1983); Satyajit Ray – honorary (1992); A. R. Rahman – 2 (2009).
- **2023:** ***Naatu Naatu*** (*RRR*, M. M. Keeravani & Chandrabose) – Best Original Song; ***The Elephant Whisperers*** (Kartiki Gonsalves) – Documentary Short.
- **2025 (97th):** *Anora* – Best Picture; Sean Baker – Director; Adrien Brody & Mikey Madison – acting.
- **Cannes (France) – Palme d'Or:** 2024 *Anora*; 2025 *It Was Just an Accident* (Jafar Panahi). **2024 Grand Prix:** Payal Kapadia – *All We Imagine as Light*. Anasuya Sengupta – Best Actress, Un Certain Regard (*The Shameless*).
- Berlin – **Golden Bear**; Venice – **Golden Lion**; UK – **BAFTA**.
- **IFFI** – Goa (permanent venue since 2004), began 1952. **BIFFes** – Bengaluru (Karnataka Chalanachitra Academy).
- India's Oscar entry is chosen by the **Film Federation of India**. Films are certified by the **CBFC** under the **Cinematograph Act, 1952**.
